for a film which mathew mccoughney seemed to have fully locked in, DBC offers very less for a biopic of an actual man. it’s the raging homophobia - that’s slowly turned into sympathy since the community is suddenly profitable - to the enlightenment that only comes post a sacrifice of a close one (on whom the onus laid unsaid yet heavily to somehow transform a pretty aggressive character’s arc) i am not sure if this trajectory is something that woodrof deserved. or for that matter, even mccoughney who very clearly gave it his all deserved either. i also could understand why would misgendering of a transwoman probably exist in the 80s, but for a film that was made in 2013, rayon could have been played by anyone but a cis-het and rather offensive jared leto. in totality of it, i kept wanting to see the queer characters also trying to live their lives, instead of them just being miserable folks who just gather some money in order to score some drugs so they can live another day while a proudly straight protagonist makes an empire out of it. in fact, i kept waiting to see homosexuality roaring unashamed unafraid in the face of woodrof, like sure, think whatever you hold against us that’s totally your personal problem, gurl. but no, that power was never given into the hands of the characters opressed. all you get to feel towards them is sadness. as if the film never cared much for them, it’s as if they remained largely invisible, and suddenly AIDS is huge because a straight guy got it. and that’s just, sad .

O filme tem uma premissa muito interessante, retrata as consequências e preconceitos sofridos por pessoas portadoras de AIDS. Trata de temas vividos pelo personagem interpretado por McConaughey; (atuação BRILHANTE) e sua transformação ao longo do filme. é cativante assistir o personagem deixando, aos poucos, de enxergar as pessoas através dos próprios preconceitos e passando a enxergá-las como indivíduos. A relação desenvolvida com o personagem interpretado pelo Jared Letto é, pra mim, o coração do filme. os dois dão aula de atuação e o relacionamento entre os dois é a engrenagem que faz o filme funcionar. porém isso também é parte do contraponto, pois eu achei o filme um pouco chato e arrastado em certas partes, mais extenso do que devia, e como falei das atuações, o filme só é oque é graças ao elenco já que não tem nada de inventivo na direção nem nada tão memorável que valha a pena ser mencionado. Mas, é um bom filme

Assim como as pessoas desesperadas usavam ivermectina ou gás ozônio por via retal para tratar Covid, o personagem principal vai em busca de algum medicamento que prolongue sua vida. Nesse processo, quem indica o tratamento é um médico clandestino no México e o Estado é apenas um obstáculo para o cowboy estadunidense na sua luta pela sobrevivência.

Every big Hollywood film dealing with problems of the marginalized is almost always about the success of a small business owner. The starting of Dallas Buyers Club is about a man getting treated as if he's a homosexual while he wastes away, and all the problems that come with it. This regressive hick dealing with the new reality that he has been forced into. Very nice. The middle third is about him being a small business owner and his run ins with the government. And ofc making fat stacks off of sick gays. That's his calling in life. That's where he finds real success. Matthew Maccounaghey is The Wolf of AIDS street. The end tries to reel it in and ground him as a person who has experienced real growth, how the experience has changed him, has made him a more compassionate man despite the hardships he's facing. But it's too little, too late. By the point it tries to reel it in, the film is no longer about the illness or the social atmosphere or even the protagonist's struggle with the illness. An aside, Known pedophile Jared Leto as a transvestite/transgender was an interesting choice.

I initially gave this 4 stars but after reading a bunch of reviews I understand the discourse a little more. Hence I can't possibly give this higher than 3. I will say the acting is good. Something about McConaughey's delivery always gets me even if it's 'one note' at times. Jared Leto surprised me as I didn't even know it was Jared Leto for the first half of the movie. By the time I did, the movie had already transformed into the Ron being a hero and Rayon being a junkie (which was an odd tonal shift to take). At the end of the film (much like a lot of other films) the written text of what happened to the protagonist leaves the viewer with a feeling of they've watched something great. However, I cannot deny it; Jared Leto playing the role of Rayon was odd. In a see of trans-women actors that could've been chosen, somehow a straight-cis man was. His performance was great and if I hadn't read about what I saw, it would've gone right past my head. But now it's something I cannot shake off. Trying to replicate a human's struggle when you haven't experienced it even in the slightest? (man.) The movie could've benefited from better writing of the struggle but even through that it did an okay enough job I feel. Apart from all of the complaints, the movie has good pacing and I never wanted to stop it in between. It also feels more lived in, partly due to how realistic the light in the images feel and how the camera moves.

Gonna get the obvious pitfalls out the way. This film is too young to be casting a cisgender man in a trans woman’s role. Boooooo!! The directors comments on this matter prove his ignorance to the community which his film is about whether he makes it about a straight guy or not. Second of all, given that it is likely that Woodroof was actually a bisexual man himself makes it a little weird that his movie version is so homophobic during this film and it is even more lgbtq erasure when added to rayons casting. I guess it’s because it’s about a journey of acceptance so definitely adds the drama but if that was the case they should’ve made the adaptation looser, not used their real names etc. other than that, this film is emotional, narratively gripping and brilliantly performed. Mcconaughey gives one of my favourite performances ever. He incredibly skilfully gives Ron so much charisma that his downfalls can be overlooked as he makes an incredibly long journey of his homophobia and he sells his desperation and heartache so well. He also is really good at making Ron the obvious dumbass that he is but also seem incredibly intelligent and dedicated when it comes to his work where you are pleasantly surprised for the character. The supporting performances are all also very nice. I found the constant hospital vibe, through the lighting or bustle or kind of minimal and slightly dingy set design really poignant in this, you can really feel everything weighing down on the dbc at all times. The fda are satisfyingly evil. The speed at which Ron moves through his character arc varies, starting with all the slurs and such and just as you think it’s gone he shows some small signs, a little comment about sissy San Francisco judges or being clearly interested in the money a lot of the time through his gold jewellery of even keeping hold of his cash whilst giving rayon his last hug.  The bond with rayon is clear and there. I think a lot of criticisms come from rayon as a character which I don’t prescribe to. There is that Ron gives her the complete bare minimum in not treating him with absolute vitriol which she feels so happy with, and the other is that she serves no purpose other than to teach Ron a lesson. I think that her happiness with Ron’s change makes sense, as they clearly formed a bond whether Ron liked it or not and he also was clearly helping the queer community. He was very interested in the profits but he did also clearly care about his clients health. I also don’t think rayons only purpose was in teaching Ron a lesson. I think that if the film is about the determination to live, she represents the colour in that, which you can really feel when she goes to the bank in a black suit for her own funeral, looking sickly with her natural hair. I do think this film shows sensitivity to the queer community, just not nearly enough for the topic it handles which is why I stunted the stars in my rating. But if you manage to ignore that it is a gorgeous story and a wonderful arc, completely by one character and failed by another, which mcconaughey absolutely carries, not to say I didn’t think this had some really great cinematography with some wondershots as well as cool sound design. I think the constant tinnitus at one point made me say ‘wow why do they keep using this it’s getting repetitive’ but eventually I realised that it acts as a reminder whenever things are going well that health wise Ron is just as doomed as he was at the beginning, he just managed to borrow some time. A very sad film. The look on mcconaugheys face when he gets clapped by his team is heartbreaking

I watched this movie without big expectations, but I was surprised by its unexpected plot. I initially thought it would be a Western-themed queer movie, but the main character wasn’t queer. Instead, after contracting AIDS from drug use, he reflects on his life and works to help others in similar situations while building a new path for himself. Since I prefer movies with dramatic elements and strong emotional delivery, this movie wasn’t quite to my taste. The way it sustained tension for a long time to show inner changes, along with its realistic and documentary-like style, felt slow and dull to me. Nevertheless, the fact that it is based on a true story made its direct delivery of messages impressive. It’s a film that captures the life of a resilient person who truly lived such a remarkable life.
